messages:
ryan: heads-up: rolled v8.0 to canary (10%) ~09:02 PST. noticing p99 up ~180ms on seq>256 workloads, affecting a slice of hosts.
maya: saw the same on fleet dashboards — p50 looks fine, p99 tail on canary hosts jumped.
ryan: digging trace — kernel selection is flipping mid-request: gemm_fast -> gemm_fallback repeatedly. suspicious.
perfbot: perf-alert: canary v8.0 -> p99 +120ms; kv_hit_rate down ~7%; batch_size variance +32%.
tara: did v8.0 include tokenizer changes? we shipped a small subtoken joiner tweak yesterday.
ryan: yes — tokenizer now emits an extra leading space token for certain prefixes. quick hypothesis: tokenization is creating more subtokens, causing KV cache fragmentation and different batching behavior.
maya: that would increase kv miss rate and change effective batch composition. saw kv_miss_rate jump from 0.11 -> 0.18 on affected hosts.
ryan: sampled logs: `kernel_route: host=ip-10-3-44 selected=gemm_fast seq_len=512 batch=2 -> fallback=gemm_naive reason=kv_miss_latency` — kernel fallback annotated with kv latency.
tara: could also be noisy tenant — any host-level noisy processes?
maya: one noisy tenant in pool-7 with chat loop seq=64 spikes, but the timing correlates with the canary rollout windows, not just tenant.
ryan: plan: 1) revert tokenizer change on a subset of canary to A/B test, 2) enable verbose kernel_selection logs on canary hosts, 3) try increasing KV shard TTL to see if reuse improves. rolling revert now to 5% of traffic.
deploy-bot: rollback request queued for service 'tokenizer' to tag v7.9. ETA 8m.
ryan: quick perf snapshot pre-rollback: canary_hosts p99=420ms, baseline p99=300ms; kv_miss_rate=0.18 vs baseline 0.11; avg_batch_size dropped 4.1 -> 2.9.
tara: if rollback fixes kv_miss_rate and latency, tokenizer is likely culprit. otherwise we need to examine kernel selector heuristics + batcher fallthrough.
maya: added temporary tracing on batcher. seeing `batch_fallthrough` events when micro-batch seq variance > ~40% — those events line up with the p99 spikes.
ryan: I'm going to try forcing kernel pin for seq>256 & batch>=2 on a small canary to see if selector flapping is the main contributor.
perfbot: caution: pinning kernel may help tail but could worsen p50 for small seq workloads. proceed with caution and narrow scope.
ryan: rollback completed. early metrics (5m): canary p99 down to 325ms, kv_miss_rate -> 0.12. leaving enhanced logs on for 30m.
srebot: incident created: INC-2026-314 - model-rollout-seqlen-kv-frag. paging on-call if regression returns :bell:.
maya: batcher config snippet I toggled for tracing: ```batcher.hysteresis_ms=8
batcher.max_batch=16
selector.short_seq_threshold=64```
ryan: follow-up: opening PERF ticket to revise kernel selection heuristics to incorporate tokenization distribution + kv_shard locality. also will add an eval to detect tokenization-induced kv fragmentation before future rollouts.
ryan: tagging @oncall for visibility. thanks all for fast triage :thumbsup:
